question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Get into hot water
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e. **'To get into trouble'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Get into hot water"** is an English idiom that means **"to get into trouble".**
 
• **It refers** to finding oneself in a difficult or precarious situation.
 
• The phrase originated from the idea that hot water can burn or scald, implying danger or trouble.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: ***'To get into trouble'.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's examine all the options one by one:
 
 
• **To get a costly gift: **This option does not align with the idiom. Getting a costly gift is generally considered a positive event (महंगा उपहार पाना)
 
• **To reach nowhere:** This suggests that no progress or achievement has been made.(कहीं नहीं पहुंचना) It doesn't align with the meaning of the idiom.
 
• **A private end to serve:** This phrase implies having a personal or private goal to achieve, often in a somewhat selfish or secretive manner.(निजी उद्देश्य की सेवा करना)
 
 

2f:T68a,

The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**<
